holidays.name: National Hot Fudge Sundae Day
holidays.description: A day to pile ice cream high with warm, gooey chocolate fudge, whipped cream, nuts, and a cherry on top. Cold meets hot in the most glorious dessert collision imaginable.
holidays.origin: The hot fudge sundae is often credited to C.C. Brown's ice cream parlor in Hollywood, which claimed to have created it in 1906. The day itself is an unofficial food observance promoted by dessert fans and food-holiday calendars.
holidays.funFact: C.C. Brown's was said to serve its sundaes with the hot fudge on the side, in a separate pitcher, so the ice cream wouldn't melt before you were ready to dig in.

holidays.name: Culinary Arts Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the people who turn raw ingredients into edible art, and a perfect excuse to put on an apron and attempt something more ambitious than toast.
holidays.origin: Culinary Arts Day is an unofficial observance that honors chefs, cooks, and the craft of cooking. It is tied to the general growth in popularity of culinary schools and cooking shows.
holidays.funFact: The tall white chef's hat, called a toque, traditionally has 100 pleats, said to represent the many ways a chef can cook an egg.

holidays.name: World Drowning Prevention Day
holidays.description: A serious but important international day dedicated to raising awareness about drowning and promoting simple life-saving measures like swimming lessons, barriers around water, and supervision.
holidays.origin: The United Nations General Assembly adopted a resolution in April 2021 declaring July 25 as World Drowning Prevention Day, after advocacy from the Global Drowning Prevention community.
holidays.funFact: It was the first UN observance dedicated specifically to drowning, a leading cause of accidental death for children and young people worldwide.

holidays.name: Thread the Needle Day
holidays.description: A day for sewing enthusiasts to celebrate the humble art of needlework, and to challenge themselves to get that stubborn thread through the tiny eye on the first try.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance celebrated by crafters and sewing lovers, it honors the age-old skill of sewing and mending, which was once an essential part of everyday life.
holidays.funFact: The oldest known needles are over 50,000 years old and were made of bone, found in a cave in Siberia.

holidays.name: Parents' Day (Fourth Sunday of July)
holidays.description: A day dedicated to appreciating moms and dads in a way that feels like a bonus round after Mother's Day and Father's Day. It is a lesser-known holiday that is often overlooked by the greeting card aisle.
holidays.origin: In the U.S., Parents' Day was established by Congress in 1994 and signed by President Bill Clinton, to recognize the role of parents in raising children. It is observed on the fourth Sunday of July, so it falls on July 25 in some years.
holidays.funFact: South Korea also celebrates its own Parents' Day, on May 8, which combines honoring both mothers and fathers into one holiday.
